```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# Verified: Checked the rendered graph, group labels, and axis scale.

nhanes <- read_csv("examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
nhanes
```

```{r}
bmi_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(Cycle),
    !is.na(Age),
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle, IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 30)

bmi_summary
```
```{r}
# Verified: Pending visual checks of axis scale, labels, and group representation.
#AI:Needed to fix errors in ggplot code. 

corrected_plot <- ggplot(
  bmi_summary,
  aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, color = IncomeGroup, group = IncomeGroup)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean BMI by Income Group Across NHANES Cycles",
    subtitle = "Adults aged 20–80 in the classroom dataset",
    x = "NHANES Cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    color = "Income Group",
    caption = "Descriptive and unweighted NHANES classroom data; not a population estimate."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

corrected_plot

ggsave(
  "assignments/assignment05-visualization/submission/corrected-plot.png",
  plot = corrected_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Visualization Audit and Revision
The original flawed visualization contained a few misleading design choices. It displayed only the first and last NHANES cycles while claiming BMI increased steadily across every cycle. It also used a restricted y-axis from 24 to 28, which could exaggerate differences between income groups. The title implied that low income causes obesity, although the data cannot establish causation.
I revisedsed the visualization to include all available NHANES cycles, use a y-axis that includes zero, and provide neutral labels describing mean BMI by income group. I also restricted the analysis to adults aged 20–80, excluded missing observations, and retained groups with at least 30 observations. The revised graph is a descriptive unweighted summary of the classroom dataset and should not be interpreted as a causal relationship or population estimate.
